newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures open mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures open mostly higher.

text.p: Most U.S. stock index futures opened slightly higher, encouraged by stable Treasury bonds and continued bullish momentum.
September Standard and Poor's 500 futures rose to 948.50 in the first minutes of trade, after posting Globex gains overnight.

"They liked them on Globex and bonds are stable to a little higher," one S&P 500 futures trader said. "I'd like to stay long from 940.00 and above," he said, pegging upside targets of 951.00, 953.00 and 956.50.
Several traders noted any dips continue to be bought.
But one trader said the market may be prone to profit-taking so close to record territory. Sept S&Ps set a contract and all-time high at 951.75 on Friday.
The trader pegged support at last Friday's 940.80 low and at Friday's settlement of 944.90.
So far on Monday, September S&Ps remained within Friday's range, a sign that the market may be on hold ahead of this week's flood of economic news.
The data line-up was empty Monday, but traders were keen for Tuesday's second-quarter employment cost index and Friday's July payrolls report.
Also on tap are a quarterly refunding announcement, second-quarter gross domestic product, as well as New York and Chicago purchasing management data.
One firm pegged September S&P 500 fair value Monday at 5.20 points premium to cash, buy programs at 6.70 points premium to cash or wider and sells at 4.00 points premium or narrower.
At 0857 CDT/1357 GMT, Sept S&P 500s were up 1.70 pts to 946.60, Nikkei rose 175.0 pts to 20,640.0, Midcap 400s rose 0.60 to 309.70, Russell rose 0.75 to 411.00, and NASDAQ fell 2.50 to 1090.00.
